from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("The Brachistochrone Problem", [

            "Straight lines aren't always fastest."
        ])
        
        # Assets

        bead.move_to(point_a.get_center())
        
        point_b = Dot(color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(point_b, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "E5", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        straight_path = Line(point_a.get_center(), point_b.get_center(), color=YELLOW)
        
        # Bezier curve
        curved_path = CubicBezier(
            point_a.get_center(), 
            point_a.get_center() + DOWN * 1 + RIGHT * 1,
            point_b.get_center() + UP * 1 + LEFT * 1,
            point_b.get_center(), 
            color=PURPLE
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title), Create(point_a), Write(label_a), Create(bead))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(straight_path), Create(point_b), Write(label_b))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.play(Create(curved_path))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Energy conservation dictates motion.", "Potential energy converts to kinetic energy.", "Increased speed early reduces total travel time."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Conservation of Energy", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        eq_total = MathTex("E = K + U", color=WHITE)
        eq_k = MathTex("K = \\frac{1}{2}mv^2", color="#00FFFF")
        eq_u = MathTex("U = mgh", color="#FFA500")
        v_formula = MathTex("v = \\sqrt{2gh}", color=WHITE)
        
        all_formulas = VGroup(eq_total, eq_k, eq_u, v_formula).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)

        # Assets
        vehicle = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vehicle.svg")
        vehicle.set_height(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(vehicle, 'F3')

        # Velocity Vector
        velocity_vector = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5, color="#FFA500")
        velocity_vector.next_to(vehicle, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(eq_total))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["We express time as an integral.", "Time depends on path length and velocity.", "Calculus of variations finds the optimal curve."]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Formulation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        time_integral = MathTex("T = \\int \\frac{ds}{v}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(time_integral, 'A3', 'B6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Asset reference: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg

        icon1 = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg") if False else Dot(color=BLACK)
        
        self.play(Write(time_integral))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        ds_sub = MathTex("ds = \\sqrt{dx^2 + dy^2}", color="#FF0000")
        v_sub = MathTex("v = \\sqrt{2gy}", color="#00FF00")

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The solution is a cycloid curve.", "A rolling circle traces this optimal path.", "It perfectly balances distance and velocity."]
        self.setup_layout("The Solution: The Cycloid", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        eq = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial y'}\right) = \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}", color=WHITE, tex_template=TexTemplate())
        self.place_in_area(eq, 'A2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        cycloid_eq = MathTex(r"x = r(t - \sin t), \quad y = r(1 - \cos t)", color="#00FFFF", tex_template=TexTemplate())
        self.place_in_area(cycloid_eq, 'C2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.85)
        self.play(FadeIn(cycloid_eq))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        r = 0.5
        def cycloid_path(t):
            return np.array([r * (t - np.sin(t)), -r * (1 - np.cos(t)), 0])

        path = ParametricFunction(cycloid_path, t_range=[0, 2*PI], color="#FFA500")
        self.place_in_area(path, 'E2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg]
        circle_img = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg", color="#FFA500")
        circle_img.scale(0.3)
        circle_img.move_to(path.point_from_proportion(0))
        
        self.play(Create(path), run_time=2)
        # Animate the wheel moving along the path
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(circle_img, path), run_time=3)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFA500")
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Race of Curves

sections.title: Introduction: Defining the Challenge (1 minute)
sections.content: Introduce the Brachistochrone problem (from Greek 'brachistos' = shortest, 'chronos' = time). Pose the question: If a particle slides down a track under gravity between two points, what shape of path results in the minimum travel time? Contrast the intuitive 'straight line' vs. the 'curved track'.
sections.example: Visual: A particle sliding down a straight ramp vs. a curved one. The curved one surprisingly arrives first.

sections.title: Prerequisite Concept: Conservation of Energy (1 minute)
sections.content: Briefly establish the physics foundation. Using the Conservation of Energy (PE = KE), derive the velocity v = sqrt(2gh). Emphasize that velocity increases as the object drops deeper, explaining why a steep initial drop (increasing speed early) is advantageous.
sections.example: Animation: An energy bar filling up as a ball drops, showing how potential energy converts to kinetic energy.

sections.title: The Mathematical Formulation (1.5 minutes)
sections.content: Introduce the time integral: T = ∫ ds/v. Substitute the path length element ds = sqrt(1 + (y')^2) dx and the velocity v = sqrt(2gy). Highlight this as a functional, setting the stage for the Calculus of Variations.
sections.example: Visual: A glowing integral equation appearing on screen, with components mapping to specific parts of the falling ball's trajectory.

sections.title: The Solution: The Cycloid (1 minute)
sections.content: Reveal the solution: The Cycloid (the path traced by a point on a rolling circle). Explain how this curve optimizes the balance between path distance and high velocity.
sections.example: Animation: A wheel rolling along a horizontal line, tracing the path of a point on its rim, which perfectly matches the optimal track.

sections.title: Conclusion & Real-world Application (0.5 minutes)
sections.content: Summarize that the shortest path is not the straight line. Mention real-world applications like the design of roller coasters and the flight paths of birds of prey (like hawks) diving for food.
sections.example: Visual: A hawk performing a high-speed dive and a roller coaster drop, both overlaying the cycloid curve.
